question: does Pavo's audio binding and lip sync degrade with line or clip length (~>= 8-9 s)? (failed build run 40307414749, k-insight 8.42 s line in a 9 s clip, 0 of 6)
method: direct Pavo calls (0 credits, fresh exact quote each) with episode_build.request()'s exact prompt for each shot, reference storyteller-ref.jpg (ch-keeper-talk, the build's talking reference), seconds = ceil(line); the WAVs rebuilt locally with pilot_render.py voice + episode_build.py lines on plans/genesis-07-short.json (Kokoro v1.0 fp16, pinned sha256); halves cut at the sentence boundary from the same voice.wav and retimed by plan_check.talk_retime/episode_build.retime; every clip judged by lipsync_check.py (thresholds unchanged: audio >= 0.85, mouth >= 0.45, speak/pause >= 1.5, face >= 0.8; face_landmarker sha pinned). 34 generations (16 for length, 12 for H2, 6 for H3).

a-insight.text: Notice the order. Grief comes before judgment. The flood is not the story of a cold God, but of a wounded heart.

b-insight-a.text: Notice the order. Grief comes before judgment.
b-insight-a.plan_check: KEEPER_LINE_TOO_SHORT (7 words, under the 12-word rule; ~2.5-3.1 s estimated) and, as a narration line, SHORT INSIGHT_MISSING (no insight line of >= 20 words is left)

b-insight-b.text: The flood is not the story of a cold God, but of a wounded heart.

ctl-line01.prompt: k-insight (control: the E95/E98 tests' WAV under genesis-07's k-insight prompt)

d-question.arm: k-question, 0.40 s lead + 0.75 s tail (raised to 0.86 s out of the 4/5 s gap band), words retimed x1.10 to 5.55 s, 6 s clip

e-question.arm: k-question, 0.40 s lead only (its own 0.30 s tail), 4.60 s in a 5 s clip

f-question.arm: k-question, its own 0.14 s lead + 0.75 s tail, words retimed x0.94 to 4.55 s, 5 s clip

d-insight.arm: k-insight, 0.40 s lead + 0.75 s tail, words retimed x1.03 to 9.55 s, 10 s clip

g-question.arm: k-question voiced again by pilot_render at Kokoro speed 0.95 with line-01's layout (LEAD_IN 0.3 s, sentence gap, pause_after 0.2 s), tail extended to line-01's 0.615 s pad; k-question prompt

h-line01-speed1.arm: line-01's own text (genesis-06's Keeper line) voiced again by today's pilot_render at speed 1.0 with the same layout, tail extended to the 0.615 s pad; k-insight prompt (as the control)

conclusions: length is NOT the cause: the built genesis-07 lines failed at every length, 1 pass in 15 (k-close 6.55 s once); 3.55 s, 4.42 s and 4.55 s lines did no better than the 8.45 s one (audio 0.07-0.98, mouth 0.10-0.47); the halves of the split were the worst (0 of 6)

the same prompt, reference and a 7 s clip with line-01.wav passed at once with the best measures yet (audio 0.992, mouth 0.685, speak/pause 3.24): the service, the prompt (E98 pose) and the reference are fine today; what differs is the input WAV

line-01.wav (the WAV of every passing direct test, E95/E98) has 0.40 s of silence before the first word and 0.75 s after the last (5.24 s of speech in 6.385 s); every WAV episode_build lines writes is cut at the first and last word of its sentences, 0.09-0.14 s of lead and 0.21-0.36 s of tail

in every failing clip Pavo's soundtrack goes on 0.5-1.0 s after our last word up to the end of the clip (the control 0.04 s, but the passing calibration clip keeper-lipsync.mp4 0.96 s too, so that alone does not separate pass from fail); in several failing clips the line is also shifted or stretched (best fit x0.81-0.94 or 0.8-1.0 s off), which never happened with line-01.wav
retiming is not the cause either: the unretimed k-insight and k-insight-b failed like the retimed k-question, k-close and k-insight-a

E95's pad window (0.25-0.65 s from the end of the WAV to the end of the clip) was measured only on line-01.wav, whose own 0.75 s tail and 0.40 s lead were part of what passed: the rule holds on the WAV length, but the words inside it need their silence too (hypothesis H2: tested below, it fails)
next_test: H4 (proposal): find the property of the words. First offline, no generation: syllable rate, the share of open vowels, and the lip-closing consonants (b, m, p) per second of each line, against each line's pass rate so far (line-01 4 of 5 today and 4 of 10 on E98; genesis-07's Keeper lines 1 of 27). Then 3 generations each on 2 rewrites of k-question chosen by that property, against line-01 as the control
changed: nothing in the engine or the plan: length refuted (16 generations), H2 fails (12), H3 shows the speed is not the cause (6); 34 generations in all, 0 credits

h2.question: do the words need silence around them, as in line-01.wav (0.40 s before, 0.75 s after)? Built from the native line trimmed to its words (-35 dB), silence added, the words retimed by talk_retime(words, gaps=lead+tail) so the WAV is N - 0.45 s (the E95 pad); rule set beforehand: the fix only if (d) passes at least 2 of 3 on each line
h2.verdict: H2 FAILS: 0 of 12 passed; (d) 0 of 3 on k-question and 0 of 3 on k-insight. Nothing changed in the engine or the plan
findings: (d) on k-insight kept our audio every time (0.992, 0.989, 0.991; unpadded 0.275-0.867 here and 0.458-0.884 in the build), but the lips stayed at 0.39 in all three (>= 0.45 needed): the silence fixed the binding of the long line and not the lips

together with the control (line-01.wav: audio 0.992, lips 0.685 under the same prompt and reference, and 10 of 11 audio >= 0.85 in the E95/E98 tests), something else in line-01.wav makes the lips follow: probably the line itself (genesis-06's Keeper line voiced at Kokoro speed 0.95, where the build voices at 1.0) or its words
h2.next_test: H3, line-01.wav against the genesis-07 lines with everything else equal: (g) k-question voiced at speed 0.95 with line-01's silences; (h) line-01's own text voiced again by today's pilot_render path at speed 1.0 with its silences; 3 generations each, against the control's 2 of 2. If (g) passes, the fix is the Keeper voice speed (characters.json voice / VOICE) with the silences; if (h) fails, the voice path itself changed since #393

h3.question: is it the Keeper's voice speed (line-01 was voiced at 0.95, the build voices at 1.0) or the line itself? Rule set beforehand: the speed fix only if (g) passes at least 2 of 3
h3.rebuild_check: pilot_render voice on line-01's text at 0.95 rebuilds line-01.wav (6.385 s, sample correlation 0.989): it is genesis-06's Keeper line "Genesis five reads like a list of funerals. But one name breaks the pattern."
h3.verdict: the speed is not the cause: (g) 0 of 3 (audio 0.73-0.78, lips 0.34-0.36). The voice path is fine: (h), line-01's text at speed 1.0, passed 2 of 3. What separates pass from fail is the line itself (its words), not its length, its silences, its retime or its voice speed. Nothing changed
h3.next_test: H4 (proposal): find the property of the words. First offline, no generation: syllable rate, the share of open vowels, and the lip-closing consonants (b, m, p) per second of each line, against each line's pass rate so far (line-01 4 of 5 today and 4 of 10 on E98; genesis-07's Keeper lines 1 of 27). Then 3 generations each on 2 rewrites of k-question chosen by that property, against line-01 as the control

measurement.question: k-insight with the silences (d): audio 0.99 three times, mouth 0.39 three times. Lips really out of sync (a generation problem) or a landmark misreading of a bearded, hooded face (a measurement problem)?
measurement.method: lipsync_check's own functions (audio_match, lip_opening, mouth_sync), unchanged: the per-frame lip opening plotted against the clip's speech envelope; mouth crops every 4th frame with the measured inner-lip points 13/14 drawn on them; full frames at 4 fps; the control and calibration clips for comparison
measurement.verdict: a generation problem, not a measurement one. The landmarks sit on the inner lips in every crop where a face is found (the beard and hood do not move them), and smoothing changes nothing (0.376-0.394). The lips really move off the words: open, teeth showing, through the 0.4 s of silence before the first word; the widest openings of the clip (~6.8 s and ~8.4 s) fall where the voice is quiet; inside the speech the lips correlate 0.22-0.28 with it, against 0.63 for the control, whose mouth closes in every pause and opens on the syllables. Same medium shot in all of them, no cut
measurement.measurement_part: small: frames with no face found (3-13 %, filled with the mean opening) and a smile baseline with the teeth showing; neither explains 0.39 against 0.69
measurement.if_the_owner_wants_a_measurement_change_: each option is a gate change for the owner, not proposed here as the fix: (1) judge the mouth only inside the speech and interpolate frames with no face instead of the mean; (2) a learned audio-visual sync score (SyncNet-style confidence and offset, open source, CPU, no spending) beside the landmark correlation, calibrated on the clips already judged here; (3) per-word windows, the lips opening within +-2 frames of each word onset. On these three clips (1) gives 0.22-0.28, lower than today's 0.39, so it would not pass them; (2) and (3) are untested. None of them justifies lowering MOUTH_CORR_MIN without new calibration evidence
